title: Miriam Makeba
summary: Miriam Makeba, a South African singer born near Johannesburg in 1932, could not return home after her passport was invalidated and spent about 30 years in exile. In 1963 she addressed the United Nations General Assembly, urging world leaders to press for an end to apartheid; the South African government then revoked her citizenship. She returned to South Africa in 1991 and died in November 2008 after a heart attack following a concert near Castel Volturno, Italy.

uncertainty.note: Birth day agrees across Encyclopaedia Africana and Encyclopedia.com. Death is given as November 10, 2008 by Encyclopaedia Africana; the other opened pages give no death date. Start of exile: Encyclopaedia Africana says after the 1960 Sharpeville massacre; Encyclopedia.com says the passport was invalidated after the 1959 Venice premiere of Come Back Africa.

importance.justification: Sources record her 1963 appeal to the UN General Assembly against apartheid, the loss of her citizenship, about 30 years of exile and a Dag Hammarskjold Peace Prize in 1986.
